equation_request.abstract: We present an idea to convert to a unitary quantum walk any open quantum walk which is defined on lattices as well as on finite graphs. This approach generalizes to the domain of open quantum walks (or quantum Markov chains) the framework introduced by Szegedy for quantizing Markov chains. For the unitary quantum walks formulated in this article, we define the probability and the mean probability of finding the walk at a node, then derive the asymptotic mean probability.

specification.problem: Given an open quantum walk (OQW, a quantum Markov chain) on a finite graph with node set V and internal Hilbert space, specified by Kraus operators B_i^j (transition from node j to node i), construct a unitary quantum walk that generalizes Szegedy's quantization of classical Markov chains, and define the probability, time-averaged (mean) probability and asymptotic mean probability of finding the walk at a node.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction: a Szegedy-type unitary quantization of a finite-graph OQW, built from the isometry whose columns are the Kraus operators of the OQW, a reflection about its range, and a swap of two node registers. Tiny explicit instance (an assumption, since no experiment_scope was supplied): 2 nodes, 2-dimensional internal space (one qubit), Kraus operators B_0^0=I/\sqrt2, B_1^0=X/\sqrt2, B_0^1=H/\sqrt2, B_1^1=I/\sqrt2, giving a 3-qubit circuit. Outside scope: OQWs on infinite lattices, the paper's exact definition/normalization of the unitary (e.g. one-step S R_A versus two-reflection R_B R_A), the paper's specific choice of which register defines the node, any closed-form or spectral theorem the paper derives for the asymptotic mean probability, and any proofs.

equations.label: Open quantum walk (quantum Markov chain) on a finite graph
equations.latex: \mathcal{M}(\rho)=\sum_{i\in V}\Big(\sum_{j\in V} B_i^j\,\rho_j\,B_i^{j\dagger}\Big)\otimes|i\rangle\langle i|,\qquad \rho=\sum_{j}\rho_j\otimes|j\rangle\langle j|,\qquad \sum_{i\in V} B_i^{j\dagger}B_i^j=I_d\ \ \forall j\in V
equations.description: Definition of a discrete-time open quantum walk: a completely positive trace-preserving map on block-diagonal states over the nodes, with node-wise Kraus (trace-preservation) constraint.
equations.justification: Standard definition of open quantum walks (Attal–Petruccione–Sinayskiy framework) recalled from background; the abstract names the object but does not state the formula.
assumptions: Finite graph; the lattice case (infinite V) is excluded from scope.

equations.label: Kraus-operator isometry replacing Szegedy's square-root amplitudes
equations.description: Isometry from (internal, current node) to (internal, current node, next node); the isometry property follows exactly from the Kraus constraint in eq_1. For a classical chain with d=1 and B_i^j=\sqrt{P_{ij}} this reduces to Szegedy's state |\psi_j\rangle.
equations.abstract_quote: This approach generalizes to the domain of open quantum walks (or quantum Markov chains) the framework introduced by Szegedy for quantizing Markov chains.
equations.justification: Inferred: Szegedy's construction builds an isometry from \sqrt{P_{ij}}; the natural generalization to an OQW replaces the scalar amplitudes by the Kraus operators B_i^j, with isometry guaranteed by trace preservation. The paper's exact construction is not available, so this is a reconstruction, not a sourced formula.
assumptions: Register ordering internal ⊗ node1 ⊗ node2 and the role of the registers are the reconstructor's convention.

equations.label: Unitary quantum walk step (Szegedy-type)
equations.description: The walk unitary is a reflection about the range of A followed by a swap of the node registers; two such steps give the two-reflection Szegedy form W=R_B R_A with R_B=S R_A S.
equations.abstract_quote: convert to a unitary quantum walk any open quantum walk which is defined on lattices as well as on finite graphs
equations.justification: Inferred from the stated Szegedy generalization: Szegedy's walk is a product of reflections about the ranges of two isometries related by the swap. Whether the paper uses U or W (or another normalization) as its unit time step is unknown.
assumptions: Choice of U=S R_A as the elementary step (W=U^2 is the equivalent two-reflection form).

equations.label: Probability of finding the walk at a node
equations.description: Probability that a computational-basis measurement of the second node register after t steps returns node i, with the internal and first node registers traced out.
equations.abstract_quote: we define the probability and the mean probability of finding the walk at a node
equations.justification: The abstract states such a probability is defined; the specific register measured (second node register here) is the reconstructor's convention consistent with eq_2, where the last register holds the destination node.
assumptions: Node position is read from the second (destination) node register; the paper might use the first register or a symmetrized definition.

equations.label: Mean probability and asymptotic mean probability
equations.description: Cesàro time average of p_t(i) and its limit. In finite dimension, the limit exists exactly and equals the sum over distinct eigenvalues of U of the squared norm of the node-i component of the eigenprojected initial state (cross terms between distinct eigenvalues average to zero).
equations.justification: The Cesàro-mean/eigenprojector formula is a standard result for finite-dimensional unitaries; the abstract says an asymptotic mean probability is derived but gives no formula, so the paper's specific expression (e.g. in terms of OQW data) is not reproduced here.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional walk space; the Cesàro mean is the intended averaging (the abstract does not specify the averaging convention).

equations.label: Tiny explicit instance: 2 nodes, qubit internal space
equations.description: Concrete OQW on the 2-node complete graph with self-loops satisfying the Kraus constraint for each j (each pair consists of two unitaries scaled by 1/\sqrt2). The initial state is the isometric embedding of internal |0\rangle at node 0. Total circuit size: 3 qubits (internal, node1, node2).
equations.justification: No experiment_scope was supplied; this is the smallest nontrivial instance chosen by the reconstructor to make the construction concrete. The abstract does not provide any example.
assumptions: X, H denote the Pauli-X and Hadamard gates; node labels 0,1 are encoded as computational basis states of one qubit.

registers.name: internal
registers.size: 1 qubit (d=2 in the instance; \lceil\log_2 d\rceil in general)
registers.role: internal (coin-like) degree of freedom of the open quantum walk on which the Kraus operators act

registers.name: node1
registers.size: 1 qubit (n=2 in the instance; \lceil\log_2 n\rceil in general)
registers.role: first node register (current/source node j); node label j encoded as computational basis state |j\rangle

registers.name: node2
registers.size: 1 qubit (n=2 in the instance; \lceil\log_2 n\rceil in general)
registers.role: second node register (destination node i); measured to obtain p_t(i); tensor order internal ⊗ node1 ⊗ node2

specification.initial_state: |\Psi_0\rangle = A(|\xi_0\rangle\otimes|j_0\rangle) with internal state |\xi_0\rangle=|0\rangle and starting node j_0=0; for the instance |\Psi_0\rangle=(|000\rangle+|101\rangle)/\sqrt2 in order internal, node1, node2 (eq_6). Prepared from |000\rangle by the controlled Stinespring dilation U_A with U_A(|\xi\rangle|j\rangle|0\rangle)=A(|\xi\rangle|j\rangle).

steps.description: Prepare |\Psi_0\rangle by applying the dilation unitary U_A (controlled on node1, apply the Stinespring dilation of the Kraus family {B_i^j}_i to internal ⊗ node2) to |\xi_0\rangle|j_0\rangle|0\rangle.
Apply the reflection R_A = U_A (I ⊗ I ⊗ (2|0\rangle\langle0| - I)) U_A^\dagger, i.e. uncompute U_A, reflect about |0\rangle on node2, recompute U_A.
Apply the swap S of registers node1 and node2. Together with the previous step this is one walk step U = S R_A; repeat steps 2-3 t times to obtain U^t|\Psi_0\rangle.
Measure node2 in the computational basis to estimate p_t(i); repeat for t=0,...,T-1 to form the mean probability.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the node2 register after t applications of U; outcome i occurs with probability p_t(i) (eq_4). Internal and node1 registers are discarded.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate p_t(i) from outcome frequencies for each t, form the Cesàro mean \bar p_T(i)=\frac1T\sum_{t<T}p_t(i), and compare with the spectral prediction \bar p_\infty(i) computed by exact diagonalization of the 8x8 unitary U in the instance (eq_5).
assumptions: No experiment_scope supplied: the 2-node, qubit-internal-space instance in eq_6 and the 3-qubit circuit are the reconstructor's choice.

The unitary walk is reconstructed as the Szegedy-type construction U = S R_A built from the Kraus isometry A; the paper's actual construction may differ in normalization, register layout or the use of W=R_B R_A as the unit step.
Node position is defined by the second node register; the paper's definition may use a different register or combination.
Mean probability is taken to be the Cesàro time average; the asymptotic formula given is the generic finite-dimensional spectral expression, not the paper's derived result.
Only finite graphs are treated; lattice (infinite) OQWs are out of scope.
missing_information: Exact definition of the unitary walk in the paper (operator form, Hilbert space, register conventions, one- versus two-reflection step).
The paper's precise definitions of the probability and mean probability of finding the walk at a node (which register(s) are measured, averaging convention).
The paper's derived expression for the asymptotic mean probability in terms of the OQW data and its relation to OQW stationary states or spectral properties.
Treatment of OQWs on lattices (infinite node sets) and any conditions (e.g. irreducibility, homogeneity) imposed on the Kraus operators.
Any worked examples, numerical results or comparisons to classical Szegedy walks.
